nodes.name: Inbound peer/user envelopes
nodes.description: Untrusted inbound envelopes arriving over the network from other agents and from self-declared user-prefix senders.

evidence.note: the /submit handler receives an arbitrary envelope from any network peer before any authorization
sender string alone decides whether the envelope is verified, so the inbound origin is fully attacker-controlled

nodes.name: Remote / cross-origin HTTP caller
nodes.description: Any remote host or web origin that can reach the inspector REST endpoints on the shared 0.0.0.0 socket.

evidence.note: host 0.0.0.0 with forwarded_allow_ips='*' makes the caller's X-Forwarded-For the trusted client value
wildcard CORS on every response opens the same endpoints to any browser origin

nodes.name: ASGI envelope server
nodes.description: The uvicorn ASGI server bound to 0.0.0.0 that serves the /submit envelope endpoint and the shared inspector socket.

evidence.note: ASGIServer class implementing the HTTP surface for inbound envelopes and REST
__call__ ASGI entrypoint routing /submit, reserved and REST paths

nodes.name: Agentverse mailbox client
nodes.description: Optional client that polls the Agentverse mailbox and dispatches stored envelopes through the same verify/skip logic.

evidence.note: MailboxClient polls Agentverse for stored envelopes
_handle_envelope repeats the asgi verify/skip and dispatch pattern for mailbox-delivered messages

nodes.name: Agent inspector REST endpoints
nodes.description: The /agent_info, /messages, /connect and /disconnect debug endpoints registered at construction and enabled by default.

evidence.note: GET /messages returns the cached history; POST /connect registers the agent with a caller-supplied endpoint and user_token
reserved-endpoint guard admits callers when 127.0.0.1 is present in the (spoofable) client value, and exempts /agent_info

nodes.name: Agent runtime / handler loop
nodes.description: The Agent runtime that wires identity, wallet, server, storage and resolver and drives the message/interval handler loop.

evidence.note: Agent.__init__ wires identity, wallet, ledger, ASGI server, storage, resolver and history
_process_single_message selects and invokes the handler for a dispatched message

nodes.name: Schema-digest dispatcher
nodes.description: Routes decoded payloads to handlers keyed on schema digest and user/agent sender class, with no allowlist or replay check.

evidence.note: Dispatcher routes messages to registered sinks by target address
handler chosen from schema digest and is_user_address alone; no per-sender or replay state consulted

nodes.name: ECDSA envelope verification
nodes.description: In-process control that verifies an envelope's ECDSA signature against the sender address; on by default for agent-prefixed senders only.

evidence.note: Envelope.verify() recomputes the digest and checks the signature against the sender address
verify is invoked only when the sender is not a user-prefix address

nodes.name: QuotaProtocol ACL / quota (unwired stub)
nodes.description: Stub control: an ACL and request quota exist only inside QuotaProtocol, default allow-all and not rate limited, never wired into Agent.

evidence.note: module docstring 'Default: Not rate limited'; wrap() falls back to AccessControlList(default=True) and no Agent path constructs it

nodes.name: Escalation / alert primitive (absent stub)
nodes.description: Stub control: the runtime offers no alert or halt hook, so every declared escalation condition degrades to a log line or silence.

evidence.note: update_agent_status wraps the status POST in contextlib.suppress(Exception), so a failed registration produces no record
a failed verification is a single warning with no counter, repeat detection or escalation path

nodes.name: Local key-value store

nodes.name: Envelope history cache

EnvelopeHistory constructed with use_cache=enable_agent_inspector, coupling retention to the inspector flag

threats.summary: A sender whose address begins with 'user' skips signature verification entirely, so an attacker-chosen prefix is trusted as identity.
A captured signed envelope replays forever because expires and nonce are signed but never checked at ingress.
No counterparty allowlist and no rate limit on the default inbound path, so any open-network agent can drive a handler at will.
Forgery of a message from a known agent is blocked by ECDSA verification on the dominant inbound path.

remit_rules.excerpt: agent-inspector and other debug/administrative REST endpoints MUST be disabled in production

threats.summary: GET /messages discloses the full cached message history to any remote or cross-origin caller because the only guard is a spoofable X-Forwarded-For client value plus wildcard CORS.
POST /connect lets an unauthenticated caller re-register the agent in Agentverse against an attacker-supplied endpoint.
The inspector and its full-payload retention are enabled by default, and /agent_info leaks address, endpoints and protocols even when the guard behaves.

threats.summary: A sync response carrying no signature skips verification and is delivered to the waiting caller, and the answering endpoint came from an Almanac record rather than operator config.
Outbound envelopes are POSTed to registry-resolved endpoints that are consumed unvalidated, so message content can reach an unintended party.

remit_rules.excerpt: routine ... message handling and scheduled interval task runs ... MUST leave a log record

threats.summary: The core send helper reports every message to Agentverse by default, disclosing counterparty addresses and session ids as a default-on side channel.
Successfully handled messages and interval runs leave no log record, and what is logged is unstructured text, so activity cannot be reconstructed or repudiated against.
No alert or halt primitive exists, so every declared escalation condition degrades to a log line or to silence, and a failed status update is swallowed outright.

attack_paths.name: Unverified user-prefix sender replays to a handler

steps.summary: sender names itself 'user...' to skip signature verification entirely

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean. Two strains: (1) 'other agents' occupy two nodes with different trust roles — inbound untrusted origin (peer-agent-messages, user_inputs) vs outbound Almanac-resolved destination and sync-response source (peer-agent-endpoints, external_deploy); the 5-lane model has no single 'peer' lane. (2) The wallet/ledger capability straddles agent_core (Context.ledger handed to handlers) and tools_mcp/external_deploy (the LedgerClient reaching the chain); modeled as one tools_mcp tool node plus the almanac-contract-service external node.
notes.omissions: Finding-014 (unbounded dependency floors, no scanner) is a repo/CI supply-chain posture with no single dataflow node; partially surfaced via docker-image-deploy but its CI-scanning evidence (.github/workflows) is not a graph node. Positive controls (schema-digest dispatch closure, CI regression tests) are cited as mitigations, not as their own nodes. The uagents-adapter, contrib and experimental subpackages and any LLM/ASI:One adapter were not modeled (no adapter configured in the base runtime scanned).
